To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) data-driven models are more accurate than physics-based models in predicting energy consumption in smart buildings, and that b) the data-driven model that is based on a time series decomposition is the most accurate of the data driven models tested.
the energy consumption of a building can be predicted using only the data from sensors in the building and a black-box model that is blind to the physics of the problem.

(i) a black-box model is more accurate than a grey-box model in predicting energy consumption, (ii) the black-box model is better at predicting consumption in normal operation than in a state of energy efficiency, and (iii) the grey-box model is better suited for predicting the energy consumption in a state of efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to energy efficiency in buildings, which is based entirely on data.
the development of a new approach for the estimation of energy consumption in buildings.

the following: 1) the creation of a data set for energy consumption prediction, 2) the creation of models for energy consumption prediction based on the data set, 3) the comparison of the performance of the models and 4) the application of the models to predict the energy consumption during an energy efficiency campaign in a real building.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for this particular problem, the data-driven approach is superior to the physics-based approach.
the data-driven models can predict the energy consumption in a building better than the models that are based on physics.

, in this case, data-driven models can provide a better performance than grey-box models, but that the performance is highly dependent on the quality and quantity of data, and on the type of prediction problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physics of a problem can be redundant when the data is complete.
the physics of the building energy consumption can be learned from data, and this is a better approach than the traditional one, in which the physics is assumed and the data is used to calibrate it.
, in order to improve energy efficiency in buildings, the use of machine learning methods is a promising avenue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
data-driven methods, which do not include physical models, are capable of outperforming models that include physics, in the case of predicting energy consumption of buildings.
the data from the building system are now so complete that they can be used as the main source of information for the energy prediction problem.
, in the case of energy consumption prediction, the data is the new black-box.
